title: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook — Q1 2026
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for annual and quarterly budgeting, rolling forecasts, procurement and contracting workflows, and revenue recognition / billing controls. The document consolidates policy, thresholds, required approvals, and runbook-style steps teams must follow to remain compliant with finance controls and to support reliable revenue reporting.

Purpose:
- Provide a single reference for finance, procurement, legal, and engineering teams to complete common activities in a repeatable way.
- Reduce cycle time for purchases and contract execution while preserving required approvals and segregation of duties.
- Ensure revenue is recognized consistently with ASC 606 principles (performance obligations, milestones, and billing cadence) and internal reporting requirements.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference business units and subsidiaries in NA, EMEA and APAC.
- Covers capital and operating budgets, vendor procurement, contracts > $5,000, SOWs, purchase orders, and subscriptions.
- Exceptions must be routed to Finance (fp&a@redwood.ai) and Legal (contracts@redwood.ai) and documented with rationale.

Definitions:
- CapEx: capital expenditures, capitalization threshold $10,000 and useful life > 1 year.
- OpEx: operational expenses charged to the P&L.
- SOW: Statement of Work.
- RevRec: revenue recognition under company policy aligned with ASC 606.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting
1.1 Annual Budget Calendar (high level)
1. Plan kick-off: Oct 1 — FP&A issues templates and preliminary guidance.
2. Manager submissions: Oct 15 – Nov 15 — functional managers submit P&L, headcount, and capex requests.
3. Exec review & consolidation: Nov 16 – Dec 10 — Product, Eng, Sales, and GTM reviews with finance.
4. Final approval: Dec 15 — CFO & CEO sign-off; board materials prepared.

1.2 Rolling Forecasts
- Cadence: Monthly rolling forecast (12-month lookahead) with a formal reforecast every quarter.
- Owner: FP&A.
- Inputs: actuals from GL, pipeline forecasts from Sales, capacity plans from Eng, and key product launch dates.
- Acceptance criteria: variance between forecast and actuals should be reconciled each month; material gaps (>5% on spend categories or >3 headcount variance) require a variance memo.

1.3 Budget Template and Required Attachments
Required fields for each functional submission:
- Line-item description
- Expense type (OpEx/CapEx)
- Amount (annual) and quarterly phasing
- Headcount FTE, salary bands, and hire dates
- Business justification (one paragraph)
- Owner and cost-center
Attachments: vendor quotes, SOW drafts, and product/feature spec for big initiatives (> $250k).

2) Procurement procedures
2.1 Purchase thresholds and approval matrix
- < $5,000: Individual contributor approval + cost center owner. Procurement engagement optional.
- $5,000 — $50,000: Manager approval + Procurement review (procurement@redwood.ai).
- $50,000 — $250,000: Director approval + Procurement + Legal spot-check.
- > $250,000: VP approval + Procurement + Legal + FP&A sign-off.
- Capital expenditures require FP&A and accounting classification review regardless of amount.

2.2 Competitive sourcing and vendor selection
- For purchases > $50,000, obtain at least two competitive quotes. Document vendor selection rationale in the procurement system (Coupa/NetSuite).
- Critical vendors (security, infra, customer data access) require a security questionnaire and an OK from Security & Compliance prior to execution.

2.3 Purchase order and invoice flow
1. Obtain approval per threshold matrix.
2. Procurement creates PO in purchasing system and routes to vendor.
3. Finance validates GL coding and receipt of goods/services.
4. AP processes invoice payment on net terms defined in contract.

2.4 Emergency purchases
- Emergency/urgent purchases (<24h lead) may follow an expedited approval path: director-level approval + e-mail backup to procurement@redwood.ai. Documentation must be added to the procurement record within 3 business days.

3) Contracts and legal process
3.1 Standard templates and playbooks
- Use the Legal team’s approved templates: Master Services Agreement (MSA), Data Processing Addendum (DPA), Statement of Work (SOW), and Reseller Agreement. Templates live at /legal/templates.
- Deviations from standard terms (e.g., indemnity, data residency, PII access) require Legal review and an exceptions log entry.

3.2 Contract review turnaround times
- Template MSA: 3–5 business days for low-risk renewals.
- New vendor MSA with non-standard terms: 7–15 business days.
- SOW only: 2–4 business days.
- Expedited reviews: request via contracts@redwood.ai and tag as URGENT; approval expected within 48 hours where feasible.

3.3 Execution and storage
- Signing authorities: CEO for strategic agreements (> $1M lifetime value) unless delegated in signature matrix.
- Counterparty signatures executed through approved e-sign platforms (e.g., DocuSign).
- All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to Contract Repository (DocuSign + ContractWorks) and linked to the procurement record within 3 business days.

4) Revenue recognition and billing policies
4.1 Principles
- Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606: identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, and recognize as obligations are satisfied.
- Billing cadence and revrec are separate but related: billing frequency (monthly/annual/usage-based) dictates cash collection; recognition follows delivery of promised service.

4.2 Common revenue scenarios
- Hosted API subscription (fixed monthly fee): Recognize ratably over the subscription period. Billing: monthly or annual prepay.
- Usage-based API (per-token): Recognize as services are delivered; invoice monthly in arrears.
- Dedicated/Reserved capacity contracts with committed spend and discounts: allocate revenue between committed and overage components; recognize committed portion ratably if performance obligations are continuous.
- Implementation / professional services SOWs: recognize on milestone completion or over time if criteria for over-time recognition are met (e.g., customer controls asset or benefits as delivered).

4.3 Billing terms and collections
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 for SaaS customers, Net 45 for enterprise with approved credit.
- Late payment escalation: reminder at 7 days overdue, collections outreach at 30 days, hold on provisioning at 60 days unless escalated to Sales leadership.
- Credit memos and refunds must be approved by FP&A and recorded with supporting rationale.

4.4 Revenue-related controls
- All sales orders and contract values must flow into RevRec subledger and map to the general ledger.
- Monthly close checklist includes: contract intake completeness, deferred revenue rollforward, and reconciliation of billed vs recognized revenue.
- Threshold for manual review: any contract increase or amendment > $100k must be reviewed by RevRec owner (accounting@redwood.ai).

5) Roles & ownership
- FP&A: overall ownership of budgeting calendar and rolling forecasts.
- Procurement: vendor sourcing, PO issuance, and vendor master data.
- Legal: contracts templates, negotiations, and signature authority.
- Accounting / RevRec: recognition policy, monthly close, and revenue rollforwards.
- Business unit managers: budget owners, first approvers for purchases, and assurance of project deliverables.

6) Common templates and examples (links)
- Budget template (spreadsheet): /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/budget-template-2026.xlsx
- Purchase request form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/purchase-request-form
- Contract deviation request form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-deviation-request-form

7) Controls, monitoring, and reporting
- Monthly: finance distributes budget vs actuals; variance commentary required for >10% month-over-month changes.
- Quarterly: reforecast workshop with Product, Eng, and Sales; re-alignment of headcount plan if hiring pace deviates by >3 FTEs vs plan.
- Yearly: internal audit snapshot of top 50 vendor contracts and procurement compliance.

8) Exception handling and escalation
- Material exceptions to policy (thresholds, single-source procurement, contract indemnity changes) require a documented exception request, Legal sign-off, and CFO approval.
- Any suspected fraud or data exposure via vendor must be escalated to Security & Compliance and Finance immediately.

Appendix A — Approval matrix (quick reference)
| Amount | Approver(s) | Procurement required? | Legal review? |
|---|---:|:---:|:---:|
| < $5k | Manager | Optional | No |
| $5k–$50k | Manager + Procurement | Yes | No (spot-check) |
| $50k–$250k | Director + Procurement | Yes | Yes |
| > $250k | VP + Procurement + Legal + FP&A | Yes | Yes |

Appendix B — Quick checklists
Budget submission checklist:
1. Complete budget template with quarterly phasing.
2. Attach vendor quotes or SOWs for line items > $50k.
3. Confirm headcount plan and hire dates.

Procurement checklist for manager:
1. Validate need and check existing contracts for preferred vendors.
2. Obtain approvals per matrix.
3. Submit PR to Procurement and attach quotes.

Contact & escalation list:
- FP&A: fp&a@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Legal / Contracts: contracts@redwood.ai
- Accounting / RevRec: accounting@redwood.ai
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.ai

Change history:
- 2025-11-05: Created by Asha Patel (initial playbook).
- 2026-01-18: Added emergency purchase expedited path and updated PO timelines (review by Liam O'Connell).
- 2026-02-10: Updated revrec thresholds and added review owners for contract amendments.

Notes:
- This playbook is intended as the authoritative internal process for the topics above. Teams requiring client-specific deviations must document exceptions and consult Legal and Finance in advance.
